description: Compress tool outputs, logs, files, and RAG chunks before they reach the LLM. 20% fewer tokens for coding agents, 60-95% fewer tokens for JSON, same answers. Library, proxy, MCP server.

summary.one_liner: Headroom is a local compression layer that shrinks tool outputs, logs, files, RAG chunks and conversation history before they reach an LLM, offered as a Python/TypeScript library, an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible proxy, and an MCP server.
summary.what_it_does: Headroom sits between an agent or app and the LLM provider and compresses content by type: SmartCrusher for JSON, CodeCompressor for source code via AST handling for several languages, and a Kompress-v2-base model for prose. A ContentRouter picks the compressor, and CacheAligner flags volatile content that would break a provider KV-cache prefix without rewriting prompts. Originals are cached locally under CCR so the model can call headroom_retrieve for full text. It can be used as an inline compress(messages) call in Python or TypeScript, as a drop-in proxy on a local port, or via headroom wrap for supported coding agents. The README also describes cross-agent memory, a headroom learn command that writes corrections into agent instruction files, and optional output-token reduction through a system-prompt verbosity note. Benchmarks in the README show 21% to 57% savings on four MCP-style scenarios and a 0.21 ms p50 compression time on a 10K-token JSON result.
use_cases: reduce token usage for coding agents like Claude Code or Cursor
compress large JSON tool results before sending to an LLM
shrink log output in agent sessions
lower API costs on long conversations
add compression to a LangChain or LiteLLM app
run a local OpenAI-compatible proxy that trims prompts
share memory across several coding agents
how_to_run: from headroom import compress; result = compress(messages, model="gpt-4o")
notable: Runs locally; the README states no prompt or file content is sent to a third party for compression
Reversible compression (CCR): originals are cached locally and retrievable on demand via headroom_retrieve
Wraps many agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Aider, Cline, Goose and others) with one command and an unwrap to undo it
Live-zone design keeps the frozen prompt prefix byte-identical so provider prompt caching still hits
Ships a Python library, a TypeScript SDK, a proxy, an MCP server and Docker image from one project
caveats: Savings depend heavily on the payload; the README says prose and already-dense output compress very little, and the 20% headline is for coding agents
Telemetry beacon is on by default (can be disabled with HEADROOM_BEACON=off, HEADROOM_TELEMETRY=off, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or HEADROOM_OFFLINE=1)

Some platform limits: native wheels cover macOS Apple Silicon and Linux; Intel macOS needs a manual ONNX Runtime setup; x86 without AVX2 falls back to non-ONNX paths; Copilot Windows login requires a separate command
